feed.subtitle: Combined Cloudflare feed: the Cloudflare Blog, the developer Changelog, Community top topics, Status incidents, and Cloudflare Research publications.

entry.title: Using AI to chart a course for our post-quantum migration
entry.content: We’re building CryptoLabe, an internal AI-powered tool that discovers cryptography across our codebase, surfaces dependencies, and helps us progress toward a full post-quantum migration by 2029. Here’s what we’ve learned so far.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Building a certificate authority for the whole Internet
entry.content: Twelve years after launching Universal SSL, Cloudflare is applying to become a certificate authority. By combining an established root, an ACME-first approach, and Merkle Tree Certificates, we are building a post-quantum CA for the open web.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Adaptive application security for the AI era: how Cloudflare connects code, traffic, and intelligence to stop attacks
entry.content: Cloudflare introduces an adaptive security framework connecting risk discovery, agent governance, runtime protection, and AI-powered response in a continuous learning loop.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Building a post-quantum certificate authority with Merkle Tree Certificates
entry.content: As post-quantum signatures threaten to inflate TLS handshakes and certificate transparency logs, Merkle Tree Certificates offer a path to compact, auditable authentication. Cloudflare’s new certificate authority will support MTC issuance at scale.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: We tested our own WAF with frontier AI models. Here’s what we found
entry.content: We built a WAF tester that adapted each request based on what the WAF blocked or passed. This helped us explore variations that a fixed test might miss. We ran it across six attack categories on an authorized staging environment and discovered detection gaps worth fixing. Here’s how the loop worked, what got through, and what we did about it.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Introducing Threat Signals: agentic skills for open-source threat intelligence, free for every Cloudflare account
entry.content: We are expanding access to Cloudforce One's Threat Events Platform to every Cloudflare account and introducing Threat Signals. Threat Signals automatically parses open-source threat reporting, extracts structured indicators, and connects threat context directly to your WAF rules.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Is your domain using post-quantum encryption? Now you can see for yourself
entry.content: Cloudflare has added visibility into post-quantum (PQ) encryption in TLS 1.3 directly into HTTP Analytics, Log Explorer, and Logpush. Learn how to make sure your domain is protected with PQ encryption.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Enforce positive security with Cloudflare Application Profiles
entry.content: Cloudflare learns the structure of your HTTP requests and identifies deviations. You can add a positive security layer that helps reduce attack surface as AI makes it easier for attackers to generate and vary payloads.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Preventing quantum downgrade attacks against IPsec
entry.content: A sophisticated attacker with a quantum computer can exploit a protocol design flaw to downgrade post-quantum IPsec tunnels to classical crypto. We helped the IETF develop a transcript authentication extension to prevent these attacks.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Cache - Invalidate cached content instead of purging it
entry.content: You can now invalidate cached content instead of purging it. Invalidation marks matching content as stale. On the next request, Cloudflare revalidates the content with your origin. If your origin responds with 304 Not Modified , Cloudflare reuses the cached content instead of downloading it again. Use invalidation to refresh a group of assets when only some of them have changed. For example, invalidate all content that shares a cache tag. Cloudflare reuses unchanged assets instead of downloading
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Changelog

entry.title: 1.1.1.1 - RFC 8509 root key trust anchor sentinel support
entry.content: 1.1.1.1 now supports RFC 8509 ↗︎ root key trust anchor sentinels. They let you check whether the responding resolver trusts a DNSSEC root key ahead of a key rollover. To check for KSK-2024 (key tag 38696), query DNSSEC-signed names in dnstest.dev : # On a sentinel-aware resolver that trusts KSK-2024: # Returns NOERROR with an A answer. dig @1.1.1.1 root-key-sentinel-is-ta-38696.dnstest.dev. A +noall +comments +answer # Returns SERVFAIL without an answer. dig @1.1.1.1 root-key-sentinel-not-ta-386
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Changelog

entry.content: Cloudflare's new Bot Preference Sync automatically aligns your robots.txt file with your AI bot policies for Search, Agent, and Training. Easily manage which bots access your content without maintaining static files.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: From all-or-nothing to task-based OAuth consent
entry.content: Cloudflare OAuth now supports optional scopes, giving users more control over what an app can access and helping developers build secure consent flows around the task at hand.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: A revisit of remote Spectre attacks on Cloudflare Workers
entry.content: In 2024 and 2025, we reassessed remote Spectre attacks on our Workers infrastructure. We share details about the new attack primitives like Spectre gadgets, remote timers, achieving co-location and how new defenses further harden Cloudflare Workers.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: BGP Role model: tracking the adoption of RFC 9234
entry.content: RFC 9234 lets routers reject route leaks on their own, using BGP Roles and the Only to Customer attribute. We measured who has deployed it, and found two Tier 1 networks unexpectedly stripping OTC.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: How Cloudflare detects MCP traffic and helps secure it
entry.content: Cloudflare Gateway identifies MCP requests using protocol-level heuristics. Security teams can use that signal to find shadow MCP traffic, enforce Portal-only access for approved servers, and block direct connections on managed network paths.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Secure all your internal vibe-coded applications — in one click
entry.content: Introducing Cloudflare Access for Workers. Attach an Access policy directly to a Worker and it applies everywhere that Worker runs — routes, custom domains, workers.dev, and previews — automatically.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Total eclipse of the Internet: traffic impacts in Iceland, Spain, and Portugal
entry.content: Cloudflare's data shows a clear impact on Internet traffic from Iceland to Spain and Portugal, following the path of totality of the total solar eclipse that occurred on August 12, 2026.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Certificate Transparency Monitoring is now generally available
entry.content: Cloudflare's Certificate Transparency Monitoring is now generally available. The biggest change: we no longer email you about certificates Cloudflare issued for your domain, so when an alert lands in your inbox, it's worth a look.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report H1 2026: 1 Tbps attacks soar as DNS floods and geopolitical tensions drive a new wave
entry.content: In the first half of 2026, Cloudflare detected a 519% surge in hyper-volumetric DDos attacks across its network. These attacks were driven heavily by DNS and CLDAP reflection vectors. This report breaks down how major geopolitical conflicts reshaped the global cyber threat landscape.
entry.dc:creator: Cloudflare Blog

entry.title: Everything we launched during Agents Week
entry.content: Our latest Agents Week has come to a close. Here’s a recap of all the announcements we made from Wallets to Radar.

entry.title: Serving the most critical missions: Cloudflare for Government achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) Certified status
entry.content: Cloudflare for Government achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) Certified status. We also announce our commitment to pursue DoD IL4 authorization. Cloudflare brings world-class security, performance, and developer products to the public sector.

entry.title: Unveiling good and bad behaviors on the Agentic Internet
entry.content: Cloudflare is shifting bot mitigation from point-in-time Risk assessment to continuous Trust evaluation. Learn how new good and bad behaviors from bots and agents are assessed by our systems, including BotBase and Precursor — and try out our Precursor Trace simulation to see how your own cursor movements would be assessed as human or bot.
